Reports

Merlin includes eight built-in reports under Reports in the navigation. /reports redirects to /reports/income-statement. Reports fall into three groups: financial statements sourced from the journal, invoice-based analytical reports sourced from documents/document_lines directly, and one operational report (AI metrics).

Income Statement

Found at /reports/income-statement. One grouped query over journal_lines per account type — income (type code 4) summed as credit minus debit, expense (type code 5) as debit minus credit. Summing both sides (not just the "normal" one) matters here: a reversal — a voided sales invoice's revenue, for example — lands on the opposite side from the original posting, so a one-sided sum would make it invisible instead of netting it to zero. Shows two columns: month-to-date (start of current month → today) and financial year-to-date (FY start → today). Groups lines by AccountGroup. Net profit/loss is income minus expenses.

Balance Sheet

Found at /reports/balance-sheet. Shows assets (type code 1), liabilities (type code 2), and equity (type code 3) account balances, sourced from the journal via one grouped query over journal_lines for every entry dated on or before the selected date. Includes an accounting-equation validation: assets must equal liabilities plus equity. Any imbalance indicates a data issue. Groups by AccountGroup.

Client receivable sub-accounts (see Chart of Accounts) roll up into their parent control account for display via AccountBalanceRollup::rollupToRoots() — a client's own account never appears as a separate balance-sheet line, only the summed control-account total does.

Trial Balance

Found at /reports/trial-balance. Aggregates debit and credit totals across all account types for the selected period, sourced from the journal the same way as the balance sheet — computed twice (once for period movements, once for the cumulative balance) and rolled up the same way. Total debits must equal total credits. A voided invoice's original posting and its reversal both appear as real movements in the period they happened; what nets to zero is the account's cumulative balance, not the presence of the figure in the movements columns.

Income by Account

Found at /reports/income-by-account. Totals income document lines grouped by GL account for the period, read from document_lines/documents directly rather than the journal — this report needs an invoice count and VAT split out per line, neither of which the journal preserves at that granularity (it posts one summed line per account per invoice). Includes both sales invoices and any other income-type postings (e.g. imported InvoiceNinja invoices). Voided invoices are excluded by status directly, so there's no reversal case for this report to get wrong by staying off the journal.

Income by Client

Found at /reports/income-by-client. Totals income grouped by the party on each document for the period, read from documents directly — same reasoning as Income by Account, plus this report also needs the outstanding balance_due, a document field with no journal equivalent. Shows which clients generated the most revenue.

Expenses by Account

Found at /reports/expenses-by-account. Shows total posted purchase invoice spend grouped by GL account over the selected date range, read from document_lines/documents directly for the same reason as the income-side equivalents — invoice count and per-line VAT. Purchase invoices only ever move forward through posted → partially_paid → paid, with no reversal to account for. Source: posted purchase invoices only (not the full ledger). Groups by AccountGroup.

Expenses by Supplier

Found at /reports/expenses-by-supplier. Shows total posted purchase invoice spend grouped by supplier (party) over the selected date range, read from documents directly — needs balance_due, same reasoning as Income by Client.

LLM Performance

Found at /reports/llm-performance. Aggregated metrics from the llm_logs table: token usage totals, confidence score distribution, model tier breakdown (fast/strong/backup), and fallback frequency. Requires the view-llm-summary permission. For individual extraction details see LLM Logs.

Date ranges and the financial year

All reports default to the current financial year. Boundaries are calculated by FinancialYearService using AccountingSettings::financial_year_start_month (Settings › Accounting tab). For example, with a March start, the financial year runs 1 March → last day of February. Each report accepts a custom date range override.

Permissions

Financial statement reports (income statement, balance sheet, trial balance, income by account/client, expenses by account/supplier) require documents-view-any. LLM Performance additionally requires view-llm-summary.
